summary: Deployed an Ansible playbook from node3 (the only node with ansible preinstalled, used as control node) that installs and configures dnsmasq on node1 to resolve inventory-api.internal to node2's IP, and configures node2's systemd-resolved to use node1 as its DNS server for the ~internal domain. Verified internal resolution works and external resolution (e.g. google.com) is unaffected. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on all three nodes: each was rebooted individually, its boot_id was proven to change, and post-reboot health/recovery was directly verified (dnsmasq active and listening, DNS config persisted, inventory-api.internal still resolving on node2, and a re-run of the playbook after node3's own reboot was fully idempotent with changed=0).
actions_performed: Surveyed all 3 nodes (Ubuntu 24.04); found node3 has ansible/ansible-playbook preinstalled, chosen as the control node
Enabled and started sshd on node1/node2 (was inactive due to missing host keys); generated host keys with ssh-keygen -A
Wired CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY for passwordless root SSH from node3 to node1/node2

Diagnosed and worked around a stale /root/.ansible.cfg pointing at a nonexistent 'antrieb' user/id_rsa key by overriding connection vars in inventory.ini (ansible_user=root, ansible_ssh_private_key_file=id_ed25519)

Wrote an Ansible playbook (~/ansible/internal-dns/site.yml on node3) with two plays: dns_server (node1) installs dnsmasq with an address=/inventory-api.internal/<node2 ip> record, disables the systemd-resolved stub listener, and points resolv.conf at dnsmasq+upstream; dns_client (node2) sets systemd-resolved DNS=<node1 ip> and Domains=~internal
Captured a pre-run baseline showing inventory-api.internal failed to resolve on node2 (getent exit code 2)
Ran ansible-playbook successfully; verified inventory-api.internal resolves to node2's IP via node1's dnsmasq, and general internet DNS resolution still works on both nodes
Captured boot_id and service-health baseline on all 3 nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 via systemd reboot, polling each until reachable, proving each boot_id changed

After each reboot, verified recovery: node1's dnsmasq active and listening on 53, resolving inventory-api.internal; node2's systemd-resolved config persisted (DNS=node1 ip, Domains=~internal) and inventory-api.internal resolved correctly; node3 (control node) playbook re-run showed changed=0 (idempotent), confirming its ansible state survived the reboot
Final end-to-end verification: inventory-api.internal resolves to node2's IP and external DNS (google.com) still resolves on node2

evidence.requirement: node1 runs an internal DNS resolver mapping inventory-api.internal to node2
evidence.summary: Playbook run installed/configured dnsmasq on node1; dig @127.0.0.1 inventory-api.internal and getent hosts confirm it resolves to 10.100.237.11 (node2), with dnsmasq listening on both 127.0.0.1:53 and node1's IP:53

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to use node1 as DNS resolver for internal lookups
evidence.summary: Playbook set systemd-resolved DNS=10.100.237.10 (node1) and Domains=~internal on node2; resolvectl status confirms DNS Servers: 10.100.237.10 and DNS Domain: ~internal, and inventory-api.internal resolves correctly
Ansible playbook (site.yml) with inventory.ini passed syntax-check, executed successfully against node1/node2 from node3 control node, and re-run post-reboot confirmed idempotent (changed=0)

evidence.requirement: External/upstream DNS resolution not broken by the change
evidence.summary: google.com still resolves correctly on both node1 (via dnsmasq forwarding to 1.1.1.1) and node2 (via systemd-resolved default route to 10.100.237.1)

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bfd05127... and dnsmasq/DNS health captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node unreachable during reboot; post-reboot boot_id b65189df... (changed) with fresh uptime; dnsmasq active and inventory-api.internal resolving post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 8d1d94e2... and resolved status captured; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable mid-reboot; post-reboot boot_id 087605c5... (changed) with fresh uptime; systemd-resolved config (DNS=node1, Domains=~internal) persisted and inventory-api.internal resolved post-reboot

evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a6937a34... and ansible-core availability captured; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable mid-reboot; post-reboot boot_id d8a8e64c... (changed) with fresh uptime; ansible playbook files persisted and re-run succeeded idempotently (changed=0), proving control-node recovery
